svg.title: Different Gaussian scales produce heavier-than-Gaussian tails
svg.desc: Illustrative example, not experimental data. Left: three equally weighted, zero-mean Gaussian components with standard deviations 1, 2, and 4 divided by the square root of 7. Right: their mixture (solid blue), compared with a Gaussian of the same mean and variance (dashed orange). Both have variance one. Shaded regions mark residual magnitudes above three. Tail probability is 1.576 percent for the mixture and 0.270 percent for the Gaussian. An inset magnifies the right tail over residuals 2.8 to 5. The component panel uses a different vertical scale for legibility. Finite Gaussian mixtures are not power-law-tailed distributions.
